newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Hussein says extremists dictate peace agenda.
newsitem.headline: Hussein says extremists dictate peace agenda.

text.p: Jordan's King Hussein said on Monday that extremists now dictate Arab-Israeli negotiations and lack of progress in peace talks could result in "great harm" to all sides.
"Extremists have dictated the agenda now and we have moved away from all the hopes and aspirations we have," Hussein told Israel Channel Two in an interview.

Asked about the peace process under right-wing Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, elected in May, Hussein said: "We certainly are concerned that progress is not as rapid as it should have been for whatever reason."
Something must be done to ensure that we continue building on what we have laid in the way of foundations, otherwise great harm can occur and great losses to all of us."
Hussein blamed the stalled peace talks on extremists from all sides whom he said had hurt the level of confidence between the parties.

He cited the 1994 Hebron massacre of 29 Arab worshippers by a Jewish settler, a spate of Moslem suicide bombings in Israel that killed 59 people nine months ago and the assassination of Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin last year by a right-wing Jew.

"Unfortunately so we came through a period of time when extremist terrorist actions, be they the Hebron massacre or the bombings in Jerusalem and elsewhere in Israel, and finally the assassination of Yitzhak Rabin. These have dictated on us a new agenda," he said.
Despite his concern, Hussein pledged to continue to work towards advancing Arab-Israeli peace talks. Jordan signed a peace treaty with Israel in 1994.
"I will do everything I can to achieve the objective I have committed myself to. To leave this world a better one, to leave this legacy behind of us peace between our peoples," he said.
